about: The recorded profile behind tests/test_intake_outbox_batch_perf.py (-m perf): the latencies its fakes sleep, each with where it was measured. 'measured' is a number read off the real system; 'derived' is computed from measured numbers; 'assumed' has no measurement yet and is the first thing a recorded batch timings block (bh-17g6b: the timings object in the --json of labels sync, labels approve --batch and outbox send-approved/send) replaces. Update a figure here when a real batch measures it, and keep its source.

store_read_s.source: bh-25fvb, 2026-11-09: GET issue median over 80 reads on the factory's Beads service, read-only (p90 94 ms)

store_listing_s.source: bh-25fvb, 2026-11-09: the outbox listing of 135 documents on the factory's Beads service

scratch_read_s.source: bh-25fvb: GET issue on a disposable scratch hive (bd init --server + bd serve, bd 1.3.0)

scratch_write_s.source: bh-25fvb: metadata compare-and-set on the scratch hive, 64-68 ms; the factory's own service was never written to

store_write_s.source: bh-25fvb: scratch_write_s x store_read_s / scratch_read_s (the factory/scratch read ratio), about 124 ms; replaced the 150 ms the bh-pc9rf model assumed

cli_write_s.source: a bd set-state subprocess; never measured. The first figure a real batch's timings block (phases.store_write) should replace

github_request_s.source: bh-25fvb: GET issue with a reused client 263 ms (348 ms with a fresh client, the pre-0.35.8 default); the per-command client of bh-vy7dx is the default from 0.35.8

github_token_s.source: bh-25fvb: gh auth token, 70 ms per call, once per GitHub operation unless the opt-in per-invocation cache keeps the first

host_check_s.source: bh-25fvb: the intake lock's host check and epoch read in one evaluation, 1.6-1.9 s per hold on the factory (13.5-14.3 s before)

process_s.source: bh-lwz8a, 2026-11-10: the process floor (wall clock less the verb) of the import-lazy outbox/thread/labels path on the factory, median 3.31 s over 5 runs of the read-only bh work outbox show --open --json (3.11-3.62 s, host load about 20), interleaved with 0.35.7 at a median 4.89 s; the effective-config load and the root callback remain. Before: bh-25fvb's 4.4 s (bh work outbox show <id> 5.3 s end to end less about 1.2 s of verb; about 2.9 s of CLI imports plus 1.4 s for the effective-config SQL load)

before_0_35_3.source: bh-25fvb: the factory on 0.35.3, 2026-11-06 (single send: 13 s of host check plus the process)

observed_0_35_5.source: bh-womf3, 2026-11-10: measured on the factory on 0.35.5 (labels sync over 135 issues, a dry run and a real one, 34 s; one send-approved of 1 labels.change 17 s end to end). The model below puts a single send at about 8-9 s, so it is optimistic by about 2x until a real batch's timings block says where the rest goes

budget_s.source: the modeled totals with headroom at batch_recheck_seconds=300 (about 56 s draft, 46 s approve, about 210 s send paced at 80 write requests a minute (bh-eqtxv; 175 s unpaced with the per-command client and field definitions of 0.35.8), 6.8 s single send with the import-lazy intake verbs of bh-lwz8a, 7.9 s before): the bar the -m perf run holds; the single send is over its 3 s target and followed up on bh-wmmfo
